title: Studying with friends
examples: Is it better to study alone or with friends?
How can we make sure we are actually learning things?
What is the best way to quiz each other?

explain.say: When you study with friends, you can quiz each other on topics.
One way to quiz is to use flashcards for vocabulary words.
Another method is to explain a concept to your friend.
You can also create practice questions together for a subject.
In real life, studying for a big test is like this group work.
A common mistake is just reading notes aloud to your friends.

faq.q: Does studying with friends always help me learn better?
faq.a: It can help a lot because you can explain things to each other. Sometimes, though, it can be distracting if you do not focus. You might also ask, 'Is group work always good for studying?' or 'Will my friends help me learn?'

faq.q: How do we make sure we are actually remembering the facts?
faq.a: You should quiz each other using different methods like flashcards. This forces your brain to actively recall the information. You could also ask, 'What is the best way to test our memory?' or 'How do we check if we know it?'
asks: What's the best way to test our memory?
How do we check if we know it?

faq.q: Should we just read the textbook chapter together?
faq.a: Reading together is okay, but it is not the best method alone. You must switch to active methods like quizzing. You could also ask, 'Is just reading enough?', or 'What should we do after reading?'
asks: What should we do after reading?

faq.q: What if one person in the group knows less than the others?
faq.a: The group should work together to help that person understand the topic. Everyone needs to take turns teaching and being taught. You might ask, 'What if someone is struggling?', or 'How do we help a friend learn?'
asks: How do we help a friend learn?

faq.q: Can we use online tools to quiz each other?
faq.a: Yes, many websites and apps have built-in quiz features. These tools provide instant feedback, which is very useful. You could also ask, 'Are apps good for studying?', or 'Where can we find quizzes online?'
asks: Where can we find quizzes online?

facts: Quizzing requires active recall, which strengthens memory.
Explaining a concept to someone else proves you understand it.
Group study works best when roles are shared fairly among members.

quiz.say: If you are studying for history, what is the most active way to quiz a friend?
quiz.show: Write the main causes of World War One.

options.show: Having the friend recite the causes from memory.
options.say: Having the friend recite the causes from memory.

options.show: Just looking at the list together.
options.say: Just looking at the list together.

quiz.why: This forces the friend to actively recall the specific facts.

wrong.0: Mind mapping is good, but reciting is a stronger test.
wrong.2: This is passive and does not test memory retrieval.
wrong.3: Reading aloud is often memorization, not recall.

quiz.say: When teaching a math concept, what is the best group activity?

options.show: Having one student teach the steps to another.
options.say: Having one student teach the steps to another.

options.show: Working through the problems side by side.
options.say: Working through the problems side by side.

quiz.why: Teaching requires you to organize and explain the concept clearly.

wrong.0: Looking at answers is not the same as solving it yourself.
wrong.1: Discussion is good, but a concrete explanation is better.
wrong.3: This shows you how to do it, but not if you know it.

quiz.say: Which study method is the least effective for long-term memory?

options.show: Teaching the material to a friend.
options.say: Teaching the material to a friend.

quiz.why: Highlighting feels productive but does not force your brain to retrieve the information.

wrong.1: Flashcards require you to actively recall the answer.
wrong.2: Teaching is one of the best ways to solidify knowledge.
wrong.3: Making questions forces you to understand the core ideas.
